name: Street Custom 'Last Meal' Emergency Ration Fabricator
product_name: Street Custom 'Last Meal' Emergency Ration Fabricator
description: A compact device that converts organic waste material — food scraps, plant matter, even paper — into edible nutrient bars through a process of sterilization, chemical breakdown, and reconstitution with added vitamins and binding agents. The Last Meal produces food that is nutritionally complete, bacterially safe, and texturally consistent regardless of input material. It does not taste good — operators describe the output as 'edible cardboard with a chemical aftertaste' — but it sustains life indefinitely from materials that would otherwise be garbage. The device has become essential equipment in Tier 1 where food security is not guaranteed.

specifications.info: plant matter; paper; approximately 400 calories per 100g input; kills all pathogens

story_hooks: Last Meal fabricators have been distributed free in a Tier 1 district by an anonymous benefactor — the devices work perfectly, but the vitamin supplement capsules contain a tracking compound.

A modified Last Meal has been developed that produces nutrient bars with psychoactive compounds — the food itself is being used as a drug delivery mechanism in communities where people eat whatever is available.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian desktop device resembling a toaster-oven hybrid with aggressive angular edges. Matte charcoal housing with visible internal chamber behind reinforced polycarbonate window. Design prioritizes function over aesthetics — industrial, unadorned, built to survive heavy handling.
physical_description.dimensions: 28cm wide × 22cm deep × 18cm tall; roughly equivalent to a microwave but more compact
physical_description.weight_description: 1.5 kg; handheld but with carrying handle molded into top panel; designed for portable workspace mounting
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed aluminum frame with impact-resistant polymer housing; internal processing chamber lined with stainless steel
physical_description.finish: Matte powder-coat charcoal with fine abrasion marks from field use; scuffed aluminum trim showing underlying metal; anti-microbial coating visible as slight iridescent sheen under direct light
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with accent strips of industrial orange along top edge; status indicator ring glows cyan when idle, shifts to acidic yellow during processing
physical_description.interface_elements: Single rotary input dial on lower right (material density selector); three-button cluster (START/STOP, BATCH COUNTER, VITAMIN BLEND TOGGLE); LED strip running vertical along left edge showing battery charge; circular button-press release for output tray; small mono LCD screen (3cm) displaying process timer and remaining charges
distinctive_features: Transparent processing chamber window allows visibility of material conversion; contents appear to roil and crystallize
Modular input hopper with translucent ribbed design — removable for cleaning organic residue
Segmented output tray with six individual bar-slots; bars eject automatically when pressed
Venting grill on rear emits faint thermal shimmer and faintly acrid chemical smell during operation
Heavy-duty power connector rated for solar or drone-dock charging — proprietary multi-pin design
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Street Custom logo (angular SC monogram) embossed on top; regulatory compliance stamps for GLMZ Tier waste-processing certification; serial number etched on rear panel; small warning label in faded yellow text: 'REPEAT: THIS DOES NOT TASTE GOOD'
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually appears worn — dust accumulation around vents, organic residue dried on hopper edges, scratches across polycarbonate window from improper cleaning, power connector shows oxidation from frequent dock cycles, surface scratches indicating field repairs with industrial sealant tape
